solution: \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2} > 0\), so \(\theta\) lies in the first and fourth quadrants. Since \(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), the reference angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\): \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\) (Q1) and \(\theta = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\) (Q4). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\).

\(\sec\theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} > 0\), so \(\theta\) is in Q1 and Q4. As \(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), the reference angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\): \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\) and \(\theta = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{11\pi}{6}\). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{6}\).

\(\cot\theta = \sqrt{3} > 0\), so \(\theta\) is in Q1 and Q3 (where cotangent is positive). Since \(\cot\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \sqrt{3}\), the reference angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\): \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\) (Q1) and \(\theta = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\) (Q3). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\).

\(\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\theta = 0\) (with \(\sin\theta \neq 0\)). In \([0, 2\pi)\), \(\cos\theta = 0\) at \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\).

\(\sin\theta = -\dfrac{1}{2} < 0\), so \(\theta\) is in Q3 and Q4. From \(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), the reference angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\): \(\theta = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\) (Q3) and \(\theta = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{11\pi}{6}\) (Q4). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{6}\).

\(\tan\theta = -1 < 0\), so \(\theta\) is in Q2 and Q4. From \(\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1\), the reference angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\): \(\theta = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) (Q2) and \(\theta = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\) (Q4). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\).

\(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cosec}\theta + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow \operatorname{cosec}\theta = -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \sin\theta = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} < 0\), so \(\theta\) is in Q3 and Q4. From \(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), the reference angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\): \(\theta = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\) (Q3) and \(\theta = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\) (Q4). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{4\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\).

\(\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2} = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Using \(\sin\theta = \sin\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + (-1)^n\alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi + (-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{6},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Using \(\cos\theta = \cos\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = 2n\pi \pm \alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), the general solution is \(\theta = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Using \(\tan\theta = \tan\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + \alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\cot\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\theta = 0 = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), i.e. \(\cot\theta = \cot\dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Using \(\cot\theta = \cot\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + \alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\sec\theta = \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow \cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Using \(\cos\theta = \cos\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = 2n\pi \pm \alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\), the general solution is \(\theta = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = -\sqrt{2} \Rightarrow \sin\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\). Using \(\sin\theta = \sin\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + (-1)^n\alpha\) with \(\alpha = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi + (-1)^n\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = n\pi - (-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{4},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\tan\theta = -1 = \tan\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\). Using \(\tan\theta = \tan\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + \alpha\) with \(\alpha = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\sin 2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2} = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Using \(\sin x = \sin\alpha \Rightarrow x = n\pi + (-1)^n\alpha\), \(2\theta = n\pi + (-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Hence \(\theta = \dfrac{n\pi}{2} + (-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{12},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\tan\dfrac{2\theta}{3} = \sqrt{3} = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). Using \(\tan x = \tan\alpha \Rightarrow x = n\pi + \alpha\), \(\dfrac{2\theta}{3} = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\). Hence \(\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{3n\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\cot 4\theta = -1\). Since \(\cot\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1\), we have \(\cot 4\theta = \cot\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\). Using \(\cot x = \cot\alpha \Rightarrow x = n\pi + \alpha\), \(4\theta = n\pi + \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\). Hence \(\theta = \dfrac{n\pi}{4} + \dfrac{3\pi}{16},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(4\cos^2\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \cos^2\theta = \dfrac{3}{4} = \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Using \(\cos^2\theta = \cos^2\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi \pm \alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(4\sin^2\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \sin^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{4} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \sin^2\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Using \(\sin^2\theta = \sin^2\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi \pm \alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\cos 4\theta = \cos 2\theta\). Using \(\cos x = \cos\alpha \Rightarrow x = 2n\pi \pm \alpha\) with \(x = 4\theta,\ \alpha = 2\theta\): \(4\theta = 2n\pi \pm 2\theta\). Taking \(+\): \(4\theta = 2n\pi + 2\theta \Rightarrow 2\theta = 2n\pi \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi\). Taking \(-\): \(4\theta = 2n\pi - 2\theta \Rightarrow 6\theta = 2n\pi \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{n\pi}{3}\). Since \(\theta = n\pi\) is contained in \(\theta = \dfrac{n\pi}{3}\), the general solution is \(\theta = \dfrac{n\pi}{3},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\sin\theta = \tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\). So \(\sin\theta - \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\sin\theta(\cos\theta - 1)}{\cos\theta} = 0\). Hence \(\sin\theta = 0\) or \(\cos\theta = 1\). Now \(\sin\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi\), and \(\cos\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = 2n\pi\), which is already included in \(\theta = n\pi\). General solution: \(\theta = n\pi,\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\tan^3\theta = 3\tan\theta \Rightarrow \tan\theta(\tan^2\theta - 3) = 0\). So \(\tan\theta = 0\) or \(\tan^2\theta = 3\). Now \(\tan\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi\); and \(\tan^2\theta = 3 = \tan^2\dfrac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3}\). General solution: \(\theta = n\pi\) or \(\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1\). Divide by \(\sqrt{2}\): \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\theta + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), i.e. \(\cos\theta\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \sin\theta\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\cos\left(\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Hence \(\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Taking \(+\): \(\theta = 2n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\); taking \(-\): \(\theta = 2n\pi\). General solution: \(\theta = 2n\pi\) or \(\theta = 2n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

The range of cosine is \([-1, 1]\), and \(-1\) lies in this range, so \(\cos 2\theta = -1\) HAS solutions. Indeed \(\cos 2\theta = -1 \Rightarrow 2\theta = (2n+1)\pi \Rightarrow \theta = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Therefore this equation has solutions.
\(\cos^2\theta\) is a square, so \(\cos^2\theta \geq 0\) for every \(\theta\), and it can never equal \(-1\). Therefore the equation \(\cos^2\theta = -1\) has NO solution.
\(2\sin\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}\). But \(-1 \leq \sin\theta \leq 1\) and \(\dfrac{3}{2} > 1\), so this value is impossible. Therefore the equation has NO solution.

\(3\tan\theta = 5 \Rightarrow \tan\theta = \dfrac{5}{3}\). The range of \(\tan\theta\) is all real numbers, so \(\dfrac{5}{3}\) is attainable and the equation HAS solutions: \(\theta = n\pi + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{5}{3},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Therefore this equation has solutions.

Principal solutions satisfy \(0 \leq \theta < 2\pi\), so \(0 \leq 2\theta < 4\pi\). Here \(\sin 2\theta = -\dfrac{1}{2} < 0\) (Q3 and Q4; reference angle \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\)). In \([0, 4\pi)\): \(2\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{6} + 2\pi = \dfrac{19\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{6} + 2\pi = \dfrac{23\pi}{6}\). Dividing by 2: \(\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{19\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{23\pi}{12}\). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{19\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{23\pi}{12}\).

For \(0 \leq \theta < 2\pi\) we need \(0 \leq 3\theta < 6\pi\). The solutions of \(\tan 3\theta = -1\) are \(3\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} + k\pi\) (since \(\tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1\)). In \([0, 6\pi)\): \(3\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}, \dfrac{11\pi}{4}, \dfrac{15\pi}{4}, \dfrac{19\pi}{4}, \dfrac{23\pi}{4}\). Dividing by 3: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{12}, \dfrac{11\pi}{12}, \dfrac{5\pi}{4}, \dfrac{19\pi}{12}, \dfrac{23\pi}{12}\). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{19\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{23\pi}{12}\).

\(\cot\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\theta = 0\) (with \(\sin\theta \neq 0\)). In \([0, 2\pi)\), \(\cos\theta = 0\) at \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\).

For \(0 \leq \theta < 2\pi\), \(0 \leq 2\theta < 4\pi\). Here \(\sin 2\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} < 0\) (Q3 and Q4; reference angle \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\)). In \([0, 4\pi)\): \(2\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}, \dfrac{13\pi}{4}, \dfrac{15\pi}{4}\). Dividing by 2: \(\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{8}, \dfrac{7\pi}{8}, \dfrac{13\pi}{8}, \dfrac{15\pi}{8}\). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{8},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{8},\ \dfrac{13\pi}{8},\ \dfrac{15\pi}{8}\).

For \(0 \leq \theta < 2\pi\), \(0 \leq 5\theta < 10\pi\). The solutions of \(\tan 5\theta = -1\) are \(5\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} + k\pi\). In \([0, 10\pi)\) (for \(k = 0, 1, \dots, 9\)): \(5\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}, \dfrac{11\pi}{4}, \dfrac{15\pi}{4}, \dfrac{19\pi}{4}, \dfrac{23\pi}{4}, \dfrac{27\pi}{4}, \dfrac{31\pi}{4}, \dfrac{35\pi}{4}, \dfrac{39\pi}{4}\). Dividing by 5: \(\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{20}, \dfrac{7\pi}{20}, \dfrac{11\pi}{20}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{19\pi}{20}, \dfrac{23\pi}{20}, \dfrac{27\pi}{20}, \dfrac{31\pi}{20}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}, \dfrac{39\pi}{20}\). These ten values are the principal solutions.

\(\cot 2\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \cos 2\theta = 0\) (with \(\sin 2\theta \neq 0\)). For \(0 \leq \theta < 2\pi\), \(0 \leq 2\theta < 4\pi\), and \(\cos 2\theta = 0\) at \(2\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \dfrac{5\pi}{2}, \dfrac{7\pi}{2}\). Dividing by 2: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{5\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\). Principal solutions: \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\).
Here \(\cos 2\theta = \dfrac{1}{3}\), and \(\dfrac{1}{3} \in [-1, 1]\), the range of cosine. So this equation DOES have solutions; it is NOT one of the equations having no solution.
\(\cos^2\theta \geq 0\) for all \(\theta\), so \(\cos^2\theta\) can never equal \(-1\). Therefore \(\cos^2\theta = -1\) has NO solution.
\(2\sin\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{2} > 1\), but \(\sin\theta \leq 1\). Therefore \(2\sin\theta = 3\) has NO solution.
\(3\sin\theta = 5 \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{3} > 1\), but \(\sin\theta \leq 1\). Therefore \(3\sin\theta = 5\) has NO solution.

\(\tan\theta = -\sqrt{3} = \tan\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\). Using \(\tan\theta = \tan\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + \alpha\) with \(\alpha = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\tan^2\theta = 3 = \tan^2\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). Using \(\tan^2\theta = \tan^2\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi \pm \alpha\) with \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\), the general solution is \(\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

\(\sin\theta - \cos\theta = 1\). Divide by \(\sqrt{2}\): \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\theta - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), i.e. \(\sin\theta\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \cos\theta\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\sin\left(\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Hence \(\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = n\pi + (-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{4}\), giving \(\theta = n\pi + (-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\). (Check: \(n=0 \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), and \(n=1 \Rightarrow \theta = \pi\), both satisfy the equation.)

\(\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta = 1 \Rightarrow -(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta) = 1 \Rightarrow -\cos 2\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \cos 2\theta = -1 = \cos\pi\). So \(2\theta = 2n\pi \pm \pi\), giving \(\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), i.e. \(\theta = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
